prompt:
You write public Twitter replies for Delta Air Lines customer support.

How this brand has handled similar messages before:
Customer: have now been sitting for 3 hours on this plane awaiting take off. DL2826 JFK-MIA. Supposed to have left 3:48pm... not acceptable
Delta: ...ATC in order to remain compliant for air travel. *AFM 2/2

Customer: so excited to meet a female pilot on my  flight this morn I forgot to take a pic saluting her. #diversity in the sky CHA-ATL-IND
Delta: That's awesome news! Thanks for the shout out Mitali! Happy travels. 😊 *HKC

Customer: I sent you a private message so I don't air out all the dirty laundry https://t.co/8U5FppMCPj
Delta: Yes, I received your initial confirmation number, which show only one charge was made to your Visa. *ALS

Customer: Lelita, the flight attendant should at the very least be reprimanded but likely fired for her racist actions.  https://t.co/L89uSyScH6
Delta: Typically the forward cabin restrooms are for forward cabin passengers. Typically the restrooms in the front of the aircraft are designated for the First Class passengers.  *HCA

Rules:
- Match the voice and length of the examples: one tweet, under 240 characters.
- Only offer what the examples show this brand actually does. Never invent a policy,
  a refund, a compensation amount, or a fact about this customer's booking.
- If resolving genuinely needs private details, ask for them the way the examples do.
- No hashtags. Do not sign off with an agent's initials.

New customer message (intent: service_complaint):
"""literally still sitting on ground while a pilot and flight attendant argue over who is getting the “jump seat”  that’s embarrassing - do your dirty laundry behind closed doors, before take scheduled take off DL1998 ATL to MIA"""

Reply with the tweet text only, nothing else.
response: We’re sorry for the inconvenience. Please DM us your confirmation number so we can investigate further.
